chapter: Opening and New Orleans trumpet players
title: Edward Clem and Joe Howard: straight players who could get hot
summary: Punch describes Edward Clem and Joe Howard as straight trumpet men who could still get hot.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Edward Clem, did you meet him?
Edward Clem, yeah. I met him too, yeah.
What was he like, Edward Clem?
Oh, you mean in his plane?
Oh, he's one of them good Dixon man men.
Didn't he sound like anybody else in Petit Park?
Well, not to my idea. Him and Joe Howard played something on the order. Mm-hmm. Remember Joe Howard? Yeah, sure. He played on that same order.
Would you describe him as a ratty trumpet player or a straight trumpet player?
No, straight. He was a straight man.
Oh, you got a straight man.
Yeah, that's right. He played a little too. Played with the Robo Show.
Now what did he play like? Was he straight or hot or what?
He was just, well he'd get hot, he used to get hot, but he was the first trumpet man. He played straight, but he got hot all right. He got hot.
